overall_assessment: Anonymization works well for UiB: e-mails (studierettleiar@...), the FSKLI901 'Emneansvarlig <name>' line and most reading-list date boilerplate are removed, and no course content was lost. All 8 name_like flags are false alarms (Adam Smith, David Hume and method names are subject matter). One real PII leak: a person's name on its own line under the 'Administrativt ansvarlig' heading, a label the role rules do not cover. The reading-list date rule also leaves fragments and misses a few wording variants.

findings.description: A staff member's name is left in course_plan as the value of the 'Administrativt ansvarlig' field. Elsewhere this field holds a unit ('Det psykologiske fakultet', 'Institutt for ...'), but here it names a person. The rubric requires names of contact persons and staff to be removed.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: 'Administrativt ansvarlig' is not in .staff_roles in R/anonymize.R, so neither .role_heading_name_regex nor .role_name_line_regex matches a name on the line under this heading. .anon_uib() has no rule for it either.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add 'administrativt ansvarlig' (and 'administrativt ansvarleg') to the heading alternatives of .role_heading_name_regex. Alternatively, in .anon_uib() remove the line after '^Administrativt ansvarlig
' when it matches .names_regex alone on the line ((?!Det|Den ...) already protects units). Add a test case in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R for 'Administrativt ansvarlig
Kari Nordmann' and for 'Administrativt ansvarlig
Det psykologiske fakultet' (kept).

findings.evidence:
Litteraturliste
Juni for haustsemesteret og 1. januar for vårsemesteret.
findings.description: The reading-list date rule removes only the start of the sentence, so a fragment is left: 'Juni for haustsemesteret og 1. januar for vårsemesteret.' (HTEK101) and '... språkvariasjon. for haustsemesteret' (ENG120). The leftover is admin dating that reads wrongly.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .anon_uib(), the date body '(?:\d\.(?=\d|[ \t]+\p{Ll})|[^.\n])*\.' lets a dot after a digit continue only before a lowercase letter, so '1. Juni' (capitalised month) ends the match at '1.'. In ENG120 the match stops after '01.07.', probably because a non-breaking space (not in [ \t]) separates it from 'for haustsemesteret'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the .anon_uib() Litteraturlist regex use '\d\.(?=\d|\h+\p{L})' (any letter, \h for horizontal whitespace including NBSP), and add tests for 'innan 1. Juni for haustsemesteret og 1. januar for vårsemesteret.' and '01.07.\u00a0for haustsemesteret'.

findings.evidence: Litteraturlista vil vere tilgjengeleg på uib.no 1. juni for haustsemesteret og 1. desember for vårsemesteret.
findings.description: Variants of the reading-list publication-date sentence that .anon_uib() is meant to strip are left in: 'vil vere tilgjengeleg på uib.no 1. juni ...' (AHKR391) and 'Litteraturlista vil normalt vere klar innan 1. juni.' (PRPSYK301C). The same sentence is removed in other courses, so the text differs between courses for no reason.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The .anon_uib() regex requires 'vil ver[ae] klare? inn[ae]n' right after 'Litteraturlist\w*', so an inserted 'normalt' or the wording 'tilgjengeleg på uib.no' does not match.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the .anon_uib() pattern to 'Litteraturlist\w*(?: for [\p{L} ]{1,30}?)? vil (?:normalt )?(?:ver[ae] (?:klare?|tilgjengele?g)(?: på \S+)?)(?: inn[ae]n)? ' followed by the same date body. Add tests for both variants.

findings.description: A dated meeting schedule with years ('tirsdag 18.feb 2025', 'tirsdag 27.mai 2025') and room numbers is left under 'Undervisningssemester'. These are administrative logistics dates rather than course content. No person is named, so this is not personal data. The pre-pass admin_date flag on these two courses is correct.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Neither .anon_generic() nor .anon_uib() removes a weekday + date + year schedule line. The generic date-time rule needs a clock time after the year.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_uib(), remove lines matching '(?m)^(?:mandag|tirsdag|onsdag|torsdag|fredag)\h+\d{1,2}\.\h*\p{L}+\.?\h*\d{4}[^\n]*\n?'. Alternatively accept this as rare logistics and document it in data/data_notes.qmd.
